rationale.conceptual: WDA is a non-local exchange-correlation functional requiring genuine understanding of DFT beyond LDA/GGA. The implementation must correctly handle the Perdew-Wang pair-distribution function, shell partitioning, a weighted-density sum rule (two versions), and efficient evaluation of v1, v2, v3 via convolution. The method involves multiple interacting parts and non-trivial math (Eqns. 1–19), placing it well above a standard plug-in.
rationale.execution: The pipeline comprises: (i) setting up structures and generating Troullier-Martins pseudopotentials, (ii) implementing the WDA functional inside a plane-wave DFT code (ABINIT/QuantumESPRESSO), (iii) modifying the sum rule, (iv) scanning lattice constants for five materials with three functionals each (~150 DFT runs), (v) constructing frozen-phonon displacements and computing energy curves (~60 additional runs). Integrating a custom non-local functional into a research-grade DFT code and managing such a parameter sweep is a substantial engineering effort with multiple fragile handoffs.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing the Weighted Density Approximation (WDA) from scratch in a plane-wave DFT code, including non-local integrals, shell partitioning, and two sum-rule variants—a non-trivial custom functional with multiple interacting components. The execution pipeline involves modifying a complex DFT codebase, running dozens of heavy plane-wave calculations, and orchestrating lattice scans and frozen-phonon series. Both conceptual depth and engineering complexity are substantial.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Plane-wave DFT with a 132 Ry cutoff on moderate perovskite unit cells requires ~32 GB RAM per calculation; many independent runs can be serialized. Input data (pseudopotentials, atomic structures) is negligible.
